audit_findings.title: Acquired earnings may be treated as organic growth without acquisition reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.7 million of 2025 acquired revenue and $184.0 million purchase consideration; OE impact unquantified; 0%-to-8% scenario sensitivity is $884.0 million or $30.23 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: SmartCover earnings enter the OE anchor and historical growth, while its purchase price may be absent from RONTA and forecast reinvestment requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: Revenue associated with SmartCover for the eleven months ended December 31, 2025 was $ 39.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition and its inclusion in 2025 results are demonstrated, while the valuation has no defined constant perimeter. The record does not quantify SmartCover owner earnings, but the growth assumption controls a $30.23-per-share bear-to-base valuation difference. Treating acquisition-assisted growth as organic, particularly with acquisition spending excluded from reinvestment, is therefore reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 OE growth and RONTA on a constant perimeter; isolate SmartCover OE and invested purchase consideration; separately model UDlive; then rerun the 0%, 8%, and 10% cases with recurring acquisition spending included wherever acquired growth is assumed.

audit_findings.title: Customer prepayments may be counted as excess cash before their obligations are discharged
audit_findings.magnitude: $104.969 million of contract liabilities versus $95.733 million of bridge cash; $104.969 million equals $3.59 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash while forecast OE may recognize earnings on prepaid contracts without reflecting the associated deferred-revenue reversal and delivery cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: For contracts recorded as long-term liabilities, $ 97.0 million was the aggregate amount of the transaction price allocated to performance obligations that were unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied as of the end of the reporting period.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash attribution and forecast treatment remain unresolved, so an error is not demonstrated. Nevertheless, deducting the entire disclosed contract-liability balance—more than all bridge cash—would reduce base value from $87.99 to about $84.40 per share and bull value from $97.74 to about $94.15, still well below the $132.49 price. The disclosed balance therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash receipts to the $104.969 million contract-liability roll-forward and verify that projected OE reflects deferred-revenue reversals and delivery costs; classify only the supported operating-cash portion outside excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Recurring SaaS contract costs could be stripped through an amortization add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 total amortization was $23.481 million, including $14.7 million of intangible amortization and $3.5 million of internal-use software and hardware amortization, leaving approximately $5.281 million not identified by the supplied breakdown
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding contract-cost amortization back to OE without deducting recurring capitalized commissions and network-service expenditures inflates the OE anchor and every forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: The recording of assets recognized from the costs to obtain and fulfill customer contracts primarily relate to the deferral of sales commissions and network service contracts on the Company's SaaS software arrangements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that recurring SaaS contract costs are capitalized, but it does not disclose their amortization, annual additions, or whether the OE calculation added that amortization back. The unidentified amount could be several million dollars annually, while the broader $23.481 million amortization pool is large relative to $133.9 million of anchor OE. The record therefore cannot establish either the error or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contract-cost asset roll-forward showing opening balance, additions, amortization, impairments, and closing balance; map its amortization and additions to the OE calculation and rerun all scenarios if additions were omitted.

audit_findings.title: Warranty accrual growth may front-run a long-duration cash tail
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.274 million 2025 reserve increase excluding the $0.607 million acquired provision, equal to 3.2% of anchor OE; approximately $2.70 per share under the base valuation multiple if fully and perpetually excluded
audit_findings.mechanism: A reserve increase could enter OE as favorable working capital even though the warranty provision is already expensed and future claims consume cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The introduction of additional technology, such as our ORION cellular radios, electronic meters and registration, have generally caused our annual warranty claims rates to increase over time.
audit_findings.explanation: The growing reserve and claims tail are demonstrated, but double counting is not established without the OE workpaper. Even assuming the entire $4.274 million organic 2025 reserve increase was incorrectly treated as recurring distributable cash, the computed base-value effect is about $2.70 per share. That is small relative to the $44.50 gap between base value and the $132.49 market price and does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace warranty provisions, acquired reserves, claims paid, and reserve changes through each OE year; remove any favorable working-capital treatment of reserve growth that duplicates the provision, and continue monitoring claims by product vintage.

audit_findings.title: Some bridge cash may not be freely distributable without tax leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: $95.733 million maximum bridge exposure, equal to $3.27 per share; indefinitely reinvested undistributed foreign earnings were $11.9 million at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: A tax or trapped-cash haircut would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In general, it is the Company's practice and intention to reinvest earnings of its non-U.S. subsidiaries in those operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a foreign reinvestment policy but does not identify how much of the latest cash is foreign or the applicable leakage. Even excluding all $95.733 million of bridge cash would reduce base value only to about $84.72 per share and bull value to about $94.47, both still below the $132.49 price. Any actual tax haircut would be smaller than this full-exclusion test and would not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by legal entity and jurisdiction, minimum operating-cash requirements, prior-tax status, withholding rates, and repatriation restrictions; apply only the evidenced after-tax haircut to the bridge.
